summary: Since 15 September 2026 Thailand grants visa-free entry of up to 30 days for tourism to passport holders of 60 countries and territories, with other stays for a few nationalities under bilateral agreements, and a visa on arrival for Azerbaijani, Belarusian and Serbian citizens; everyone else applies through a single global eVisa portal, and all foreign arrivals must submit the Thailand Digital Arrival Card (TDAC) before travel.

currencyLimits.text: Leaving Thailand, you must declare Thai baht over THB 450,000 or foreign currency over USD 15,000 (or equivalent) to customs. Taking out more than THB 50,000 in baht needs permission, except up to THB 2,000,000 to Vietnam, Yunnan (China) and the countries bordering Thailand. On arrival, foreign cash above the threshold the Finance Minister sets must be declared; no official page we could read states the current arrival figure, so declare large sums.

tips.text: The UK Foreign Office says overstaying costs 500 baht a day, up to 20,000 baht, and that you risk detention, deportation at your own expense and a re-entry ban of up to 10 years.
Vapes and e-cigarettes are illegal to possess or use in Thailand — the UK Foreign Office says there are no exceptions for tourists or for personal use.

The UK Foreign Office says criticising the Thai monarchy (lèse-majesté) is illegal, that the law can be interpreted broadly and carries a long prison sentence, and that people have been charged over comments and shared articles online.
The TDAC arrival card is free. Third-party websites charging a fee for it are unnecessary. Use only tdac.immigration.go.th.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Thailand?
faq.answer: No. Since 15 September 2026, US passport holders can enter Thailand visa-free for up to 30 days for tourism. They must still submit the free Thailand Digital Arrival Card (TDAC) before travel.

faq.question: What is the TDAC and who needs it?
faq.answer: The Thailand Digital Arrival Card is a free online arrival form that every foreign national must submit within 3 days before arriving in Thailand, at tdac.immigration.go.th. It replaced the paper TM6 card.

faq.question: How much does a Thailand tourist visa cost?
faq.answer: For nationalities that need one, the single-entry tourist visa costs USD 40 and the 6-month multiple-entry visa (METV) USD 200 when applied for through the Royal Thai Embassy in Washington; other embassies charge in local currency, so the amount differs. Apply at the official portal thaievisa.go.th. Passport holders of the 60 countries and territories under the visa exemption scheme do not need a tourist visa for stays of up to 30 days.

faq.question: Can I extend my visa-free stay in Thailand?
faq.answer: Possibly. Visitors who want to stay longer can, if eligible, apply for an extension through the Thai immigration authorities before their permitted stay ends. Since 15 September 2026 the visa-exempt stay itself is 30 days.

faq.question: Is travel insurance mandatory for Thailand?
faq.answer: No, insurance is not an entry requirement for tourists, but medical treatment must be paid for, so cover is strongly recommended.
